book_title: Chapter 8: Reading the Tape — Trend, Volume & Why We Stand Aside
question: Does Mondelēz's Stage 2 chart overcome 6 distribution days, a 38.8%-breadth US Downtrend, and rejected valuation asymmetry?

epigraph.quote: A Stage 2 uptrend in an individual defensive stock cannot rescue an investment when valuation asymmetry fails and the broader market sits in a Downtrend.
epigraph.author: Stan Weinstein & Institutional Risk Desk

web_blocks.html: The US equity market sits in a Downtrend as of November 20, 2026 (only 38.8% of stocks above their 50-day SMA, with 10 index distribution days) [30]. Inside that weak tape, Mondelēz screens as a defensive Stage 2 stock. At the November 20 close of $66.28 ($66.08 on the November 23 snapshot), MDLZ holds above its key moving averages. It trades +3.53% above its 10-week EMA ($64.02 facts; $64.64 snapshot) and +5.21% above its 50-day SMA ($63.00). It also sits +6.35% above its 30-week SMA ($62.32 snapshot) and +8.64% above its 200-day SMA ($61.01).

Near-term volume shows clear institutional supply overhead. Daily RSI(14) sits at 55.97 (weekly 59.73; 4H 50.38), and Bollinger Bandwidth is a tight 9.88%. Shares rose +0.90% on November 20 on 12.07 million shares (1.43x 20-day average) before easing -0.30% to $66.08 on November 23. Even so, facts_US_2026-11-20.json records 6 stock-level distribution days in 25 sessions. Confectioners industry breadth is also weak, with only 20% above the 50-day EMA and 40% above the 200-day EMA.

web_blocks.takeaway: Despite Stage 2 alignment, 6 MDLZ distribution days, 10 index distribution days, a 38.8% breadth Downtrend, and 0.89:1–1.01:1 R:R vs $61.61 stop warrant REJECTED on both equity and options.

web_blocks.html: Our options desk confirms zero convexity edge. The scanner flagged a 53-DTE 2027-01-15 $70/$77.5 Bull Call Debit Spread at $0.58 net debit ($580.00, or 77.2 bps / 0.77% of our $75,110.60 NAV). However, its $70.58 breakeven (+6.81%) sits right against our $71.00 Base Target and above our $68.95 EV. We stamp NO_OPTIONS_EDGE (DECLINED) and keep 100% in Treasury cash.

book_paragraphs: A Stage 2 uptrend on a stock chart is a necessary check, never a blank check. When valuation asymmetry breaks down and the broader market is in a Downtrend, disciplined investors stand aside rather than forcing a trade.

Look at the broader US market as of November 20, 2026: our facts ledger flags an active Downtrend, with only 38.8% of stocks holding above their 50-day moving average and 10 institutional distribution days on the board. Inside Mondelēz's Confectioners industry group, only 20% of peers sit above their 50-day EMA. Meanwhile, Mondelēz itself closed at $66.28 on November 20 ($66.08 in the November 23 TradingView snapshot) with 6 stock-level distribution days in the last 25 sessions.

On the technicals alone, Mondelēz sits in Stage 2 above its rising 30-week SMA ($62.32 in snapshot), 10-week EMA ($64.02 in facts; $64.64 in snapshot), 50-day SMA ($63.00), and 200-day SMA ($61.01), with daily RSI at 55.97 and Bollinger Bandwidth at 9.88%. Yet against our $61.61 invalidation stop (matching the snapshot invalidation level and sitting above the prior $61.43 anchor), $66.28 offers only 1.01-to-1 reward-to-risk to our $71.00 Base Target and 0.89-to-1 to $70.42 consensus.

We also declined the 53-day 2027-01-15 $70/$77.5 Bull Call Debit Spread ($0.58 debit, or $580.00 = 77.2 bps of our $75,110.60 NAV). Requiring MDLZ to clear $70.58 (+6.81%) in 53 days just to break even—when our Base Target is $71.00 and our expected value is $68.95—offers no real edge. We stamp NO_OPTIONS_EDGE and stay in cash.

book_callouts.title: NARRATOR'S REFLECTION: When Stage 2 Tape Meets Rejected Valuation
book_callouts.quote: A clean chart cannot fix an unattractive expected value; 0.89:1 to 1.01:1 reward-to-risk in a 38.8%-breadth Downtrend is a clear pass.
book_callouts.text: Even with MDLZ holding above its 50-day and 200-day moving averages, 6 stock distribution days and 10 index distribution days leave no room to stretch valuation.

book_subsections.title: Reconciling November 20 Facts Close ($66.28) vs. November 23 Snapshot ($66.08)
paragraphs: Transparency across data feeds matters. Our verified November 20, 2026 facts ledger records MDLZ closing at $66.28 (+0.90% on 12.07 million shares), with a 50-day SMA of $63.00, 200-day SMA of $61.01, and ATR(14) of $1.45. Our live TradingView snapshot retrieved November 23 records $66.08 (-0.30%), with a 30-week SMA of $62.32, 10-week EMA of $64.64, and invalidation stop of $61.61. Across both prints, the decision is identical: REJECTED on valuation.

book_subsections.title: Why We Declined the 2027-01-15 $70/$77.5 Bull Call Spread
paragraphs: The deterministic options scanner highlighted a 10-contract 2027-01-15 $70/$77.5 bull call debit spread at $0.58 per share ($580.00 total risk, or 77.2 basis points of our $75,110.60 NAV). While the theoretical max gain of $6,920.00 looks tempting on paper, the $70.58 breakeven requires a +6.81% rally in 53 calendar days during a US Downtrend—leaving almost zero margin below our $71.00 Base Target. Declining the trade preserves 77.2 bps of capital.

book_subsections.title: Why Distribution Days and Macro Breadth Matter for Low-Beta Staples
paragraphs: Investors sometimes assume a 0.32-beta consumer staple like Mondelēz can ignore the broader stock market. History says otherwise. When our market facts ledger records a Downtrend with only 38.8% of US stocks above their 50-day moving average and 10 index distribution days over the past 25 sessions, institutional risk managers raise cash across the board—including trimming defensive winners that are up 23% year-to-date.

That institutional supply is already visible in Mondelēz own volume footprint. While Friday November 20 saw a +0.90% bounce on 12.07 million shares, the preceding 25 trading days logged 6 stock-level distribution days, and Confectioners industry breadth sits at just 20% above the 50-day EMA. Buying a stock with 0.89-to-1 to 1.01-to-1 reward-to-risk directly into overhead resistance at $68.09–$68.92 while six distribution days sit on the tape is a low-probability bet.
